newsitem.title: USA: Barrett plans deep Wyoming development well.
newsitem.headline: Barrett plans deep Wyoming development well.

text.p: Barrett Resources Corp has applied to the Wyoming Oil and Gas Conservation Commission to drill a deep test development well in the Cave Gulch field in Natrona County, Amalgamated Exploration Inc said on Friday.
The Cave Gulch Federal No. 1-29 (Lak) is scheduled to be drilled to a depth of 18,150 feet to test eight prospective pay zones from 16,000 to 18,000 feet.

Amalgamated will have a 1.46 percent working interest on the $7.6 million project. Other working interests are held by Chevron Corp, Texaco Inc, Moncrief, Mountain Petroleum, Prima Energy Corp, Yates Petroleum and others.
Amalgamated also said Utah approved a wildcat well planned by DuPont Co's Conoco Inc in the Kaiparowits Plateau in southern part of the state.
It said the planned test will drill to 14,500 feet at an estimated cost to Conoco of $2 million.
The well will be drilled adjacent to a 1,600-acre lease where Amalgamated has an overriding royalty of 0.87 percent, the company said.
